title_en: Regulations on the Protection of Olympic Symbols

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated to strengthen the protection of Olympic symbols, safeguard the lawful rights and interests of the owners of Olympic symbols, and promote the development of the Olympic movement.

Article 3 For the purposes of these Regulations, "owners of Olympic symbols" refer to the International Olympic Committee, the Chinese Olympic Committee, the institution applying to host the Olympic Games within the territory of China, and the organizing body of the Olympic Games held within the territory of China.
The division of rights among the International Olympic Committee, the Chinese Olympic Committee, the institution applying to host the Olympic Games within the territory of China, and the organizing body of the Olympic Games held within the territory of China shall be determined in accordance with the Olympic Charter and the relevant host city contract for the Olympic Games.

Article 4 The owners of Olympic symbols shall enjoy exclusive rights to the Olympic symbols in accordance with these Regulations.
Without the permission of the owners of Olympic symbols, no person may use the Olympic symbols for commercial purposes.

Article 6 In addition to the provisions in Article 5 of these Regulations, if any activity using elements related to the Olympic movement is sufficient to mislead people into believing that there is a sponsorship or other support relationship with the owners of Olympic symbols, thus constituting an act of unfair competition, it shall be dealt with in accordance with the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 7 The market supervision and administration department and the intellectual property department of the State Council shall, in accordance with these Regulations, be responsible for the protection of Olympic symbols nationwide.
The local market supervision and administration departments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with these Regulations, be responsible for the protection of Olympic symbols within their respective administrative regions.

Article 8 The owners of Olympic symbols shall submit the Olympic symbols to the intellectual property department of the State Council, and the intellectual property department of the State Council shall make an announcement thereof.

Article 9 The term of validity of an Olympic symbol shall be 10 years, commencing from the date of announcement.
The owner of an Olympic symbol may handle the renewal procedures within 12 months prior to the expiration of the term of validity, and the term of validity for each renewal shall be 10 years, commencing from the day following the expiration of the previous term of validity of the Olympic symbol. The intellectual property department of the State Council shall announce the renewed Olympic symbols.

Article 10 Any person who, with the permission of the owner of Olympic symbols, uses the Olympic symbols for commercial purposes shall conclude a license contract with the owner of Olympic symbols. The owner of Olympic symbols shall promptly disclose information such as the types of Olympic symbols licensed for use, the licensee, the goods or service items licensed for use, the time limit, and the territorial scope.
The licensee shall use the Olympic symbols within the types of Olympic symbols, the goods or service items licensed for use, the time limit, and the territorial scope as agreed in the license contract.
Article 11 Any person who has used Olympic symbols according to law prior to the coming into force of these Regulations may continue to use them within the original scope.

Article 12 Any person who, without the permission of the owner of Olympic symbols, uses the Olympic symbols for commercial purposes, or uses similar symbols sufficient to cause misidentification, thereby infringing the exclusive right to Olympic symbols and causing a dispute, the parties shall resolve the matter through negotiation; if they are unwilling to negotiate or negotiation fails, the owner of Olympic symbols or an interested party may file a lawsuit with the People's Court, or may request the market supervision and administration department to handle the matter. When the market supervision and administration department handles the matter, if it determines that the infringement is established, it shall order the immediate cessation of the infringing act, and confiscate and destroy the infringing goods and the tools mainly used to manufacture the infringing goods or to manufacture Olympic symbols without authorization for commercial purposes. If the illegal business turnover is 50,000 yuan or more, a fine of not more than five times the illegal business turnover may be imposed concurrently; if there is no illegal business turnover or the illegal business turnover is less than 50,000 yuan, a fine of not more than 250,000 yuan may be imposed concurrently. If a party is dissatisfied with the handling decision, it may apply for administrative reconsideration in accordance with the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the People's Republic of China, or may directly file a lawsuit with the People's Court in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The market supervision and administration department handling the matter may, at the request of the parties, conduct mediation on the amount of compensation for infringement of the exclusive right to Olympic symbols; if mediation fails, the parties may file a lawsuit with the People's Court in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
Any person who commits fraud or other activities by using Olympic symbols, which constitutes a crime, shall be investigated for criminal liability according to law.

Article 14 If imported or exported goods are suspected of infringing the exclusive right to Olympic symbols, the Customs shall investigate and handle the matter by reference to the powers and procedures provided in the Customs Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Customs Protection of Intellectual Property Rights.

Article 15 The amount of compensation for infringement of the exclusive right to Olympic symbols shall be determined based on the losses suffered by the right holder due to the infringement or the profits gained by the infringer through the infringement, including the reasonable expenses paid to stop the infringing act; if the losses of the infringed party or the profits gained by the infringer are difficult to determine, the amount shall be determined reasonably by reference to the license fee for the use of the Olympic symbol.
Any person who sells goods without knowing that they infringe the exclusive right to Olympic symbols, and can prove that the goods were legally obtained and indicate the supplier, shall not bear compensation liability.

Article 16 In addition to being protected in accordance with these Regulations, the Olympic symbols may also obtain protection in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations such as the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China, the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China, the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Regulations on the Administration of Special Symbols.
Article 17 The protection of symbols related to the Paralympic Games shall be implemented by reference to these Regulations.
Article 18 These Regulations shall come into force as of July 31, 2018.
